title: An empty-carrier signal aliases productive transfer and hydrolysis in the stated assembly states
status_authority: Current scientific acceptance is conferred only by exact version-bound substantive internal review overlays; physical acquisition and novelty are separate.
reported_status: For upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U-O-CO-P_n, the listed productive transfer to a downstream aminated adaptor and hydrolysis of the acyl linkage both leave the upstream carrier in state U-OH. A downstream polymerase that senses only U-OH cannot distinguish the two outcomes. Thus donor-empty is not, by itself, a completion certificate. The failure is observational: an adequate next-address rule must also read a product-qualified receiving state, or the hydrolysis leakage must be separately bounded for the intended use.

proof_availability.classification_scope: Exact indistinguishability of two supplied transition alternatives under the sole empty-donor observation. Product occupancy on the receiving carrier separates this pair, but no reaction rate, physical sensor, chemical identity guarantee or implemented assembler is established.
